subject: Bridging credit schedule — packaging corridor & partial true-up mechanics
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@orbitushealth.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: tom.reeves@orbitushealth.com, procurement@orbitushealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Order form redline + questions on bridging credit mechanics

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement/legal team reviewed the draft order form and attached a redline (OrderForm_Orbitus_v1_redline.pdf). A few items we need clarified on the pricing exhibit before we can sign: 

1) Bridging credits: the redline adds a retroactive credit for months where usage fell below committed floors during migration windows. We need to know the proposed lookback window and whether credits are applied as an offset on subsequent invoices or as a one-time payment.

2) Partial true-up mechanics: the draft language allows partial true-ups but doesn't define rounding or prorating when a customer decommissions capacity mid-quarter. Can you confirm how partial-quarters are handled and whether there's a minimum billing increment?

3) Packaging corridor / cap on credits: we proposed a soft cap equal to 25% of the quarterly commit. If you’re not comfortable with a hard cap, we’d accept a mechanism where credits are capped and then eligible for a reconciliation in the next quarter.

4) Contractual trigger for decommission protections: we redlined a decommission trigger that would waive surcharges for planned decommissions with 45 days’ notice. We want assurance that this won’t be used to bypass minimums.

We included inline comments in the PDF and a simple spreadsheet with example calculations (PricingExhibit_Bridge_20250614.xlsx). Can you review and share a proposed compromise? Ideally our procurement lead (Tom Reeves) and I would like an answer by end of week so internal approvers can move to signature.

Thanks —
Emma Liu
Head of Procurement
Orbitus Health

Attachments: OrderForm_Orbitus_v1_redline.pdf; PricingExhibit_Bridge_20250614.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@orbitushealth.com>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@orbitushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redline + questions on bridging credit mechanics

Emma — thanks for the clear notes and the examples, that helps a lot. We’ll review and come back with proposed language by Thursday. Internal plan: I’ve looped in Laura (sales lead) to align commercial compromise, Irene (legal) for contract language, and Rishi (finance) for the P&L impact.

Immediate answers to each point:
- Credits: we typically apply credits as invoice offsets (next billing cycle). If Orbitus needs a one-time payment instead, we can evaluate but will need to confirm accounting.
- Partial true‑ups: we can propose a standard prorating approach based on days in the billing period, with a floor of one day.
- Cap: open to a soft cap approach; will run scenarios.
- Decommission trigger: we can accept a 45‑day notice clause provided we define "planned decommission" and preserve minimums via a short-term surcharge or make‑good.

Would Orbitus be open to a 20–60 day true-up/lookback window (tiered by quarter) instead of a single number? If yes, we’ll propose concrete language.

Call option: happy to do a 30-minute call Wed/Thu to finalize.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redline — proposed redline language (bridging credits & decommission)

Team —

I reviewed Orbitus’s redline and the spreadsheet. Below are clean, suggested contract clauses to address the three primary items. I attached a marked-up PricingExhibit_Bridge_20250614.xlsx with examples and the PDF with inline language.

1) Bridging Credit Application: 
"Bridging Credits" shall be applied as an offset to subsequent invoices within the then-current subscription year. Bridging Credits shall be calculated on a monthly basis using the difference between the committed monthly units and actual billed units, subject to the Credit Cap defined below. If requested in writing within sixty (60) days of the invoice date, Customer may request a one-time cash payment instead of an invoice credit; Redwood reserves the right to require substantiation and to approve cash payments at its sole discretion.

2) Partial True-up and Proration: 
In the event of a decommission or capacity reduction mid-billing period, true-ups will be prorated on a per-day basis (actual days of service/total days in the billing period). Notwithstanding the foregoing, a partial-usage adjustment will not be recognized for any period shorter than three (3) days. Billing increments smaller than one full day are not recognized.

3) Credit Cap and Reconciliation: 
Customer’s Bridging Credits in any given quarter shall not exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of the Customer’s committed quarterly units ("Credit Cap"). Any credits in excess of the Credit Cap shall be deferred to the subsequent quarter and eligible for reconciliation subject to mutual agreement. 

4) Decommission Protection Trigger: 
A planned decommission shall be effective only if Customer provides written notice at least forty-five (45) days prior to the planned cessation of service and provides a migration plan. Planned decommissions shall be excluded from s. X (temporary surge surcharge) only where the migration does not materially and adversely affect Redwood’s scheduling of reserved capacity. 

Comments: these clauses aim to give Orbitus the operational protection they want while protecting Redwood’s reserved capacity economics. If Orbitus insists on cash payments rather than invoice credits as the default, we’ll need a stronger offset/approval gate and possibly a higher price to account for cash settlement risk.

I’ll prepare redline language for the order form with bracketed fields so we can send to Orbitus.

Irene
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redline — cost impact snapshot

Quick numbers for context (high level):
- Quarterly commit: 1,200,000 tokens equivalent
- 25% Credit Cap -> max credits = 300,000 tokens equivalent
- If applied as invoice offsets, expected quarterly revenue impact (run-rate) ~ $12,000 at our blended ASP.
- If Orbitus requests cash settlement on credits by default, we estimate one-time cash exposure of ~$12k per quarter plus additional working capital cost (~1–2% of nominal amount).

Recommendation: accept invoice-offset default with the 60-day cash payment request window (Irene’s language). For decommissions, keep the 45-day notice requirement but add a provision that if the decommission is part of a strategic product sunset agreed in writing, credits are limited to 15% of the quarter to avoid gaming.

If we move to a smaller lookback window (30 days) the exposure drops roughly 40% — tradeoff for Orbitus is lower protection window.

Happy to run scenario-specific numbers if you want the workbook broken down by month/region.

Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@orbitushealth.com>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@orbitushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redline + questions on bridging credit mechanics

Emma / Tom —

Thanks for sending the redline and examples. Apologies for the back-and-forth; attached are the redlined clauses and a short summary of commercial impact. High-level compromise we are prepared to offer: 

- Bridging credits applied as invoice offsets by default; Customer may request cash payment within 60 days of invoice (subject to approval).
- Credits calculated monthly and prorated per-day for mid-period decommissions; no adjustments for periods < 3 days.
- Credit Cap set at 25% of committed quarterly units. Excess credits are deferred to the next quarter for reconciliation.

To address Orbitus’s concern on decommissions being used to bypass minimums, we will add a carveout: planned decommissions tied to a vendor-approved migration plan will be eligible for protection; unilateral decommissions that materially affect reserved capacity will trigger a short-term surcharge equal to 10% of the difference for the remainder of the quarter.

If these points look acceptable, we will issue an updated order form and DocuSign envelope for signature. Alternatively, if you prefer a smaller lookback window (30 days) instead of 60, let us know and Rishi will send updated exposure numbers.

Propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow to finalize language if helpful.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_Orbitus_v1_redline.pdf; PricingExhibit_Bridge_20250614.xlsx; MutualActionPlan_Orbitus.docx
